TERM-SIMPLE-PENDULUM.label: simple pendulum
TERM-SIMPLE-PENDULUM.definition: A point-mass bob suspended from a string of negligible mass and negligible stretch; the idealised model system whose small-angle motion is simple harmonic.
indicators: bob diameter small relative to string length
string mass negligible relative to bob mass
swing confined to a vertical plane
TERM-SIMPLE-PENDULUM.distinguishing_test: Is the bob effectively a point mass on a massless string? If the body's mass distribution and moment of inertia matter, prefer TERM-PHYSICAL-PENDULUM.

sources.access_note: section text read on openstax.org on 2026-11-12 (open access textbook); not peer-reviewed research

TERM-SIMPLE-PENDULUM.claim_limit: A model-system label for a rig. It cannot certify that a real apparatus is ideal; string elasticity and pivot friction are not measured in this pack.

TERM-PHYSICAL-PENDULUM.label: physical pendulum
TERM-PHYSICAL-PENDULUM.definition: An extended rigid body swinging about a pivot, whose period depends on its moment of inertia and the distance to its centre of mass.
indicators: object size not negligible relative to swing radius
period shifts when mass distribution changes at fixed length
TERM-PHYSICAL-PENDULUM.distinguishing_test: Does the object's moment of inertia about the pivot affect the motion? If yes, this is a physical pendulum, not the point-mass model.

sources.ref: OpenStax, University Physics Volume 1, section 15.4 'Pendulums' (physical pendulum learning outcome and treatment)
sources.access_note: section text read on openstax.org on 2026-11-12 (open access textbook); the physical-pendulum subsection was seen in the section outline

TERM-PHYSICAL-PENDULUM.claim_limit: A model-system label. Choosing it does not by itself determine which corrections matter for a given rig.

TERM-PERIOD.label: period of oscillation (T)
TERM-PERIOD.definition: Elapsed time per complete oscillation, in seconds per cycle.
indicators: measured as total elapsed time divided by cycle count
unit is seconds per cycle
TERM-PERIOD.distinguishing_test: Is the quantity seconds per cycle (period, T) or cycles per second (frequency, f)? Check the unit before labelling.

sources.ref: OpenStax, University Physics Volume 1, section 15.4 'Pendulums' (period and frequency of a simple pendulum)
sources.access_note: section text read on openstax.org on 2026-11-12 (open access textbook)

TERM-PERIOD.claim_limit: A quantity label. Reporting a period does not establish what governs it.

TERM-FREQUENCY.label: frequency (f)
TERM-FREQUENCY.definition: Oscillations per unit time, in cycles per second; the reciprocal of the period.
indicators: unit is cycles per second or hertz
computed as cycle count divided by elapsed time
TERM-FREQUENCY.distinguishing_test: Is the quantity cycles per second (frequency) or seconds per cycle (period)? The two are reciprocals and must not be interchanged.

sources.ref: OpenStax, University Physics Volume 1, section 15.4 'Pendulums' (angular frequency, frequency and period)
sources.access_note: section text read on openstax.org on 2026-11-12 (open access textbook)

TERM-FREQUENCY.claim_limit: A quantity label. A frequency value says nothing about the mechanism producing the oscillation.

TERM-SMALL-ANGLE-APPROXIMATION.label: small-angle approximation
TERM-SMALL-ANGLE-APPROXIMATION.definition: The replacement of sin(theta) by theta (radians) for small angles; below about 15 degrees the two differ by less than 1%, which reduces the pendulum equation to simple-harmonic form.
indicators: all release angles below about 15 degrees
period found nearly independent of amplitude at fixed length
TERM-SMALL-ANGLE-APPROXIMATION.distinguishing_test: Are all release angles below about 15 degrees? If amplitudes are larger, or the measured period grows with amplitude, model the anharmonic correction instead.

sources.ref: OpenStax, University Physics Volume 1, section 15.4 'Pendulums' (small-angle approximation; under-1% bound below ~15 degrees)
sources.access_note: section text read on openstax.org on 2026-11-12 (open access textbook); the <1% difference claim was read in the section text

TERM-SMALL-ANGLE-APPROXIMATION.claim_limit: Valid only inside its stated angle bound. It cannot license ignoring amplitude in a large-angle experiment.

TERM-ANHARMONIC-CORRECTION.label: anharmonic (large-angle) period correction
TERM-ANHARMONIC-CORRECTION.definition: Beyond the small-angle regime the period exceeds the simple-harmonic value, with the leading correction growing as the square of the amplitude.
indicators: release angles above about 15 degrees
measured period drifts upward with amplitude at fixed length
TERM-ANHARMONIC-CORRECTION.distinguishing_test: Does the period measurably grow with release angle at fixed length? Then the plain small-angle formula underestimates T and the correction model is the right label.

TERM-RESTORING-FORCE.label: restoring force
TERM-RESTORING-FORCE.definition: The net force component directed toward equilibrium; for a pendulum bob this is the tangential component of the weight, minus m g sin(theta).
indicators: force component along the arc, directed to equilibrium
magnitude m g sin(theta) in the ideal model
TERM-RESTORING-FORCE.distinguishing_test: Is the quantity a force (newtons) or an acceleration (m/s^2)? The tangential force contains g but is not g itself.

sources.ref: OpenStax, University Physics Volume 1, section 15.4 'Pendulums' (net force minus m g sin(theta) toward equilibrium - a restoring force)

TERM-RESTORING-FORCE.claim_limit: A force label inside the ideal model. This pack contains no force measurement; a restoring-force claim here stays a mechanism hypothesis.

TERM-MEASUREMENT-UNCERTAINTY.label: measurement uncertainty
TERM-MEASUREMENT-UNCERTAINTY.definition: Quantified doubt about a measurement result, expressed as a range derived from instrument resolution and repeatability, and reported alongside the value.
indicators: value reported as x plus/minus u
u traced to resolution or repeat spread
TERM-MEASUREMENT-UNCERTAINTY.distinguishing_test: Can the stated doubt be traced to instrument resolution or repeat spread (uncertainty), or is it a consistent directional offset (systematic error)?

TERM-SYSTEMATIC-ERROR.label: systematic error (bias)
TERM-SYSTEMATIC-ERROR.definition: A consistent directional offset in measurement results, not reduced by repetition.
indicators: repeated measurements cluster tightly but off the reference value
offset persists across operators or sessions
TERM-SYSTEMATIC-ERROR.distinguishing_test: Does repetition shrink the doubt (uncertainty) or leave a persistent offset (systematic error)? Name which one the data pattern shows.

TERM-GRAVITATIONAL-ACCELERATION.label: gravitational acceleration (g)
TERM-GRAVITATIONAL-ACCELERATION.definition: Local free-fall acceleration; the scale parameter of the simple pendulum period, T = 2 pi sqrt(L/g).
indicators: reported in m/s^2
extracted from period and length through a model
TERM-GRAVITATIONAL-ACCELERATION.distinguishing_test: Is the quantity the local acceleration itself (m/s^2) or a force component derived from it? State which was measured and which was modelled.

TERM-GRAVITATIONAL-ACCELERATION.claim_limit: A g value inferred through the pendulum model is model-dependent; it is not an independent measurement of g.

THEORY-SIMPLE-PENDULUM-MODEL.label: simple pendulum model (small-angle)
THEORY-SIMPLE-PENDULUM-MODEL.statement: For release angles below about 15 degrees the pendulum equation reduces to simple-harmonic form and the period is T = 2 pi sqrt(L/g), independent of bob mass and nearly independent of amplitude.
explains: why measured period grows roughly with the square root of length
how g can be estimated from period and length
why bob mass is not expected to change the period in the ideal model
does_not_explain: energy loss through air resistance and pivot friction
whether a specific rig satisfies the ideal assumptions

THEORY-SIMPLE-PENDULUM-MODEL.claim_limit: A model relation valid within its assumptions. It does not license ignoring uncertainty or damping when fitting real data.

THEORY-DAMPED-OSCILLATION.label: damped harmonic oscillation
THEORY-DAMPED-OSCILLATION.statement: A real pendulum loses energy to air resistance and pivot friction; its amplitude decays over time and the damping slightly modifies the oscillation.
explains: why amplitude decreases across successive cycles
why long timing runs may drift relative to the ideal model
why an ideal model can fit early cycles better than late ones
does_not_explain: the size of the damping in a specific rig without measurement
whether damping or a timing artefact caused a specific discrepancy

THEORY-ERROR-ANALYSIS.label: measurement error analysis
THEORY-ERROR-ANALYSIS.statement: A measured value must be reported with a quantified uncertainty; combining resolution and repeatability bounds what a comparison of measured values can establish.
explains: how to state a measured period as a value with a range
why a difference smaller than the combined uncertainty is not a finding
does_not_explain: the source of a specific bias
whether the chosen uncertainty model is adequate for a given rig

relations.note: Reciprocals; the unit decides which label is right.
Both describe period-vs-amplitude behaviour; the release angle decides.
Spread and offset are different doubts and need different remedies.
The rig is the model system the theory describes.
The period relation is the theory's quantitative content.
The restoring force is the model's causal core; it is not measured in this pack.
g enters the period formula as the scale parameter.
The term is operationalised by the error-analysis frame; no verified source yet.
